title: Preference representation and choice theory
status: Original six-case mathematical blueprint; full authoring and separate review still required
scope_decision: Supply full finite/general-lexicographic/strict-monotone-orthant representation, rich and restricted choice correspondence results, and finite GARP/Afriat equivalence. Do not claim a general continuous representation theorem on arbitrary topological spaces.

worked_cases.title: Finite weak orders, full choices and ordinal transformations

inputs.choice_domain: All 63 nonempty subsets; choose every utility maximizer.

results.alternate_utility: u squared on range {0,1,2}, giving {0,1,4}; all certain choices unchanged.
results.lottery_boundary: Half a and half c has expected u=1, tied with sure b, but expected u-squared=2 exceeds sure b value1. Ordinal certain-choice transformations are not unrestricted expected-utility transformations.

worked_cases.title: A continuous diagonal utility without convex preferences

inputs.general_theorem: Finite-dimensional R_+^L; complete/transitive, closed weak graph and strict coordinate monotonicity.

results.shape: The midpoint of two equally ranked bundles is worse, so upper contours need not be convex. No quasiconcave representation exists for these nonconvex preferences.

worked_cases.title: The lexicographic obstruction and its finite-grid boundary

inputs.sequence: For n>=3, (1/2+1/n,0) strictly preferred to (1/2,1), but limit (1/2,0) is strictly worse.

results.nonrepresentation: Disjoint nonempty utility intervals (u(t,0),u(t,1)) indexed by uncountably many t would inject [0,1] into Q.
results.finite_code: 5i+j gives all25 distinct ranks0,...,24, agreeing with all625 ordered comparisons.
results.small_weight_boundary: No fixed epsilon>0 makes x1+epsilon*x2 represent the full square. Choose a=min(epsilon/2,1/2), then (a,0) lexicographically beats (0,1) but has smaller weighted value.

worked_cases.title: Exact rationalization from incomplete menu coverage

results.positive_rationalizers: Exactly three weak orders: a~b above c above d; a~b above d above c; or a~b above c~d. Values of normalized ranks in a,b,c,d order are(2,2,1,0),(2,2,0,1),(1,1,0,0).
results.negative: Pair-menu WARP passes but a>b>c>a prevents a transitive rationalizer. Every one of7 nonempty choices on the missing triple breaks WARP.
results.criterion: For finite complete reported choice sets, weak chosen-to-available edges with strict chosen-to-excluded edges admit an exact weak-order rationalizer iff no directed cycle contains a strict edge. Collapse weak reachability classes and order their acyclic quotient.

worked_cases.title: Budget WARP can miss a longer revealed cycle

inputs.income: Each observed own expenditure is1; full nonnegative linear budget.

results.bad_direct_edges: 1 to2,2 to3,3 to1, plus self; all three off-diagonal edges strict.
results.bad_pairwise_WARP: Passes the tie-permitting pair condition; fails GARP at three transitive strict reversals.
results.local_nonsatiation_boundary: u(x)=max(0,x1+x2+x3-2) is globally nonsatiated yet flat on every original budget, because their positive prices imply sum x<=5/4. It rationalizes even the GARP-violating observed selections, showing why global nonsatiation cannot replace the local hypothesis.

worked_cases.title: Constructive Afriat certificates and unidentified counterfactual demand

results.same_budget_extra_maximizer: For A at budget1, (0,5/4,0) also maximizes with value1; recording e1 is not observing a singleton demand correspondence.
results.new_demand_proof: For A, u<=2/3 L1+1/3 L2=-1/15+(16/15)(x1+x3)+(13/15)x2<=19/15. Equality forces full spending,x2=0,L1=L2 and hence (7/6,0,1/12); L3 is strictly slack. For B use4/5 L1+1/5 L2=-13/50+(32/25)(x1+x3)+(26/25)x2<=67/50; analogous equality gives(4/5,0,9/20).

proof_contracts.topic: Finite weak-order representation and ordinal uniqueness
proof_contracts.status: Elementary route for future authoring; not a completed chapter proof
proof_contracts.hypotheses: Finite nonempty X; complete transitive weak preference.
proof_contracts.route: Prove that indifference is an equivalence relation and that the induced order on its classes is a complete strict order. Rank the finitely many classes and assign those ranks to their members. This gives x weakly preferred to y exactly when u(x)>=u(y). Conversely a real-valued representation inherits completeness/transitivity. If v is another representation, equal u-values imply indifference and equal v-values, so define a strictly increasing transformation on the range u(X).
proof_contracts.prerequisites_to_supply: Equivalence classes and a finite ordered-class enumeration; distinguish ordinal certain-choice utility from the positive-affine restriction for expected utility over lotteries.

proof_contracts.topic: Lexicographic failure of every real-valued representation
proof_contracts.status: Elementary contradiction route; stronger than the existing V05 continuous-representation counterexample
proof_contracts.hypotheses: Lexicographic order on the full [0,1]^2, with first coordinate strictly prioritized.
proof_contracts.route: If u represented it, for each t the interval (u(t,0),u(t,1)) would be nonempty. For t<s, lexicographic order gives u(t,1)<u(s,0), so these intervals are pairwise disjoint. Choose the first rational in each interval under a fixed enumeration of Q. This injects uncountably many t into Q, a contradiction. The argument rules out any real-valued representation, not just continuous ones.
proof_contracts.prerequisites_to_supply: Density and countability of Q, uncountability of [0,1], and the explicit first-rational rule. If these facts have not been proved in prerequisites, supply their short countability/diagonal arguments.

proof_contracts.topic: A fully elementary sufficient continuous representation on the consumption orthant
proof_contracts.status: Root approved this bounded sufficient route on 9 October 2026; final theorem contract remains root-owned
proof_contracts.hypotheses: X=R_+^L for finite L>=1; the preference is complete and transitive; its weak graph is closed under simultaneous convergent sequences in X; it is strictly coordinate-monotone: x>=y and x!=y imply x strictly preferred to y.
proof_contracts.route: For each x, 0 is weakly below x and M times the all-ones vector is weakly above x when M>=max_i x_i. Along the diagonal, closed weak upper/lower cuts cover [0,M] and are both nonempty; interval connectedness (or a proved infimum argument) gives an indifferent diagonal t*1. Strict monotonicity makes this t unique. Let u(x)=t. Transitivity and the diagonal order establish exact representation. If x_n->x, the associated t_n are bounded by max_i x_ni. Every convergent subsequence of t_n has limit t with t*1 indifferent to x by closed graph, hence t=u(x). Boundedness and subsequence uniqueness give t_n->u(x), proving continuity.
proof_contracts.prerequisites_to_supply: Connected intervals or an explicit cut/infimum proof; compact subsequence theorem; treatment of x=0; definition of relative-domain continuity. No convexity of preferences or differentiability is required.
proof_contracts.general_scope_not_claimed: This does not prove the general continuous-representation theorem on every Euclidean subset without monotonicity or a diagonal path. MIT slide 17 states representation existence without proving the broader construction. Root must either retain the sufficient orthant theorem or separately supply the broader proof and its topological hypotheses.

proof_contracts.topic: Correspondence WARP on a sufficiently rich menu domain
proof_contracts.hypotheses: A nonempty C(B) subset B for every B in the menu family; every singleton, pair and triple belongs to that family. Rationalization means equality with all weak maxima.
proof_contracts.route: Use pair choices to define x R y iff x is chosen from {x,y}; nonemptiness gives completeness. WARP equates this pair relation with weak revelation from arbitrary observed menus. To prove transitivity, if x R y and y R z but not x R z, nonempty choice on {x,y,z} and successive WARP implications force choices incompatible with the pair {x,z}. For an observed menu, every chosen x is above every available y. Conversely if x is above every menu alternative, choose any z from the nonempty observed C(B); pairwise x R z and WARP imply x is also chosen. Pair choices uniquely determine the rationalizing weak order.
proof_contracts.prerequisites_to_supply: Handle ties and repeated alternatives explicitly. WARP necessity under a fixed weak order holds on any menu domain, but this sufficiency proof uses the triple domain. Do not infer existence of a maximum on arbitrary infinite menus from rationality alone.

proof_contracts.topic: Restricted finite menus and equality versus selected-choice rationalization
proof_contracts.status: Potential elementary completion criterion; final chapter design not prescribed
proof_contracts.hypotheses: Finite X and a finite family of nonempty menus with nonempty complete reported choice sets.
proof_contracts.route: Record weak edges from each chosen alternative to every available alternative, marking the edges to excluded alternatives strict. A weak-order exact rationalizer cannot have a directed cycle containing a strict edge. Conversely, if no such cycle exists, collapse mutually reachable weak-edge classes and assign ordered ranks along a topological ordering of the finite acyclic quotient. No strict edge is internal to a class. The resulting utility makes all and only the reported choices maximize each observed menu.
proof_contracts.prerequisites_to_supply: Prove finite directed reachability classes and existence of an acyclic ordering, rather than invoking an unproved graph algorithm. This is different from treating a single observed budget choice as the complete maximizing set. Pairwise WARP alone on a restricted menu family need not rule out a longer cycle.

proof_contracts.status: Original inequality proof route supported by Varian pages 946-949 and969
proof_contracts.hypotheses: Finite positive-price, nonnegative-bundle dataset with complete linear budgets and observed expenditure equal to income; utility rationalization with local nonsatiation.
proof_contracts.route: An affordable observation implies a weak utility comparison. If it is strictly cheaper, local nonsatiation supplies a nearby strictly better bundle still inside the same budget, so equality in utility would contradict maximization; this gives a strict utility comparison. Chain weak comparisons through the transitive closure. A strictly affordable reverse comparison would create a strict utility cycle, giving GARP. Conversely a GARP violation supplies a concrete cycle with a strict edge, and every such cycle violates GARP.
proof_contracts.prerequisites_to_supply: The strict slack must leave a relative-domain neighborhood inside the budget. Keep tie-permitting budget WARP, longer GARP chains, SARP and full-correspondence WARP as separately displayed conditions.

proof_contracts.topic: Constructive Afriat feasibility without an unproved linear-programming oracle
proof_contracts.status: Finite induction route checked against the actual Appendix I text and equation images
proof_contracts.hypotheses: The same finite dataset satisfies GARP; use the reflexive transitive revealed relation R.
proof_contracts.route: Among the remaining indices choose an R-maximal class E (no remaining strictly higher predecessor) and remove classes in that order; let B be previously assigned indices. At the first class take common U and lambda positive. For a later class choose U_E as the minimum of U_j and U_j+lambda_j*p^j dot (x^i-x^j) over i in E,j in B. For each such pair p^i dot (x^j-x^i)>0, since otherwise i R j and i would have been assigned no later than j. Choose a common lambda_E at least one and at least every (U_j-U_E)/(p^i dot (x^j-x^i)). This supplies inequalities in both directions between the new and old classes. Inside E the utilities are equal and GARP gives the required nonnegative cross-expenditure terms. Induct until every index is assigned. A finite common additive shift adjusts the utility levels if positive labels are desired.
proof_contracts.prerequisites_to_supply: Prove finite maximal-class existence and termination, each denominator sign, all three induction cases, and positivity of multipliers. Do not merely quote Algorithm 3 or claim an unexecuted LP proves feasibility.

proof_contracts.topic: Afriat lower envelope and all required shape/optimality properties
proof_contracts.status: Direct finite-affine proof route with the source display correction made explicit
proof_contracts.hypotheses: U_s <= U_t+lambda_t*p^t dot (x^s-x^t) for every pair; lambda_t>0 and p^t in R_++^L.
proof_contracts.route: Define u(x) as the minimum over t of U_t+lambda_t*p^t dot (x-x^t). Finitely many affine terms give continuity, and taking the minimum preserves concavity by the defining concavity inequality. For x>=y,x!=y, every affine difference is positive, with a positive minimum over the finite index set; hence u(x)>u(y), implying local nonsatiation. At an observed x^s, every term is at least U_s by the Afriat inequalities and its own term equals U_s, so u(x^s)=U_s. If x is affordable at budget s, its s-term is at most U_s, hence u(x)<=U_s. This proves rationalization without derivative or interior assumptions.
proof_contracts.prerequisites_to_supply: Do not reverse the vector difference in the source page-970 first display. Do not claim differentiability or unique demand from a minimum of affine functions. Strictly positive prices support the strict coordinate-monotonicity conclusion.

proof_contracts.status: Implementation requirements only; no chapter lab or prototype produced
proof_contracts.hypotheses: Exact finite declared dataset; explicit numeric representation and inequality convention.
proof_contracts.route: Compute direct affordability edges and their transitive closure, retaining a path for any strict reversal. A future bounded standard-library checker can verify every candidate Afriat inequality and the lower-envelope certificate independently. If presenting linear feasibility, use lambda_t>=1 after a justified common positive rescaling; allowing all-zero multipliers is invalid. Any tolerance for measured data must be a separately defined perturbed test, not silent strict-to-weak inequality changes.
proof_contracts.prerequisites_to_supply: Supply the finite reachability proof or a transparent path enumeration at the chosen bounded size. GARP success is a model-existence statement conditional on fixed preferences, observed prices/bundles and complete budgets; it is not identification of the true utility, a test of every omitted constraint, or a statistical confidence statement.

additional_full_proof_requirements: Prove Q countability/density and uncountability of[0,1] briefly if not already established. Use explicit enumeration to choose one rational per disjoint interval, and a Cantor binary-sequence/ternary injection argument to avoid ambiguous decimal expansions.

In the diagonal theorem, bound t(x) between0 and max coordinates; handle x=0, closed cut existence, uniqueness and sequential continuity completely. No differentiability or convexity assumption is imported.

For restricted menu graphs, prove reachability equivalence classes and existence of a maximal class in a finite acyclic quotient. Utility ranks decrease along chosen-to-available edges, with strictness for excluded alternatives.
Prove GARP iff absence of a weak affordability cycle with at least one strict edge. Keep budget tie-permitting WARP distinct from exact full-correspondence WARP.

In Afriat induction, choose a maximal remaining reachability class, prove positive new-to-earlier expenditure denominators, and verify prior-prior, new-prior, prior-new and within-class inequalities. Supply a tied-class example with p1=p2=(1,1),x1=(1,0),x2=(0,1),U1=U2,lambda1=lambda2=1.

The affine-envelope proof must establish continuity, concavity, strict coordinate monotonicity, exact utility labels and budget optimality. Never infer unique demand or true utility identification from feasibility. Prove both new-budget unique choices with the displayed global upper bounds.

exercise_contracts.task: Write a short theory/evidence referee report on a claim that GARP success identifies true concave preferences and validates forecast demand.
exercise_contracts.answer: 12-point rubric,2 each for observation/choice convention, budget/price assumptions, local nonsatiation, exact graph/certificate evidence, observational equivalence/counterfactual limit, and useful next evidence.
